title: Electricity sold by a town utility
intro:
Illustrative data, made up for this book. A town's utility sold this much electricity (GWh) each year from 2010 to 2023. Fit a linear trend on the year and forecast 2026.

Give the trend (GWh per year), the forecast for 2026, and the 95 % prediction interval for that one year, each to one decimal.

In the Workbench: **Simple linear regression** with **x column** *Year*, **y column** *GWh*, **Predict at x₀** 2026.

NewLower.says: That is the interval for the trend line itself. A forecast of one year's sales needs the prediction interval (New observation), which is wider.

NewUpper.says: That is the interval for the trend line itself. A forecast of one year's sales needs the prediction interval (New observation), which is wider.

hints: x is the year and y the GWh. The forecast is ŷ at x₀ = 2026, three years past the last year.
A forecast of one future value uses the prediction interval: ŷ₀ ± t(0.025, n − 2) σ̂ √(1 + 1/n + (x₀ − x̄)²/S_xx).
